title: Linear-time decoding and stripping
statement: There exist a finite Turing machine $M$ over the Boolean alphabet and a natural number $c$ such that, for every Boolean word $x$, $M$ computes the following output in at most $c(|x|+1)$ steps: if $x$ decodes as a pair $(a,v)$ and $v$ has a last occurrence of $\mathrm{true}$, return the encoding of $a$ paired with the prefix of $v$ strictly before that last occurrence; if either operation is undefined, return the empty word.
hypotheses_covered: There exist a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet
